# Javier Ponz Prado — open application to Nous Research

> An open job application. Javier Ponz is an AI systems operator and technical
> troubleshooter in Aberdeen, Scotland, applying to Nous Research for technical
> support engineering. Ten years at Apple Retail in technical diagnosis, customer
> operations and team leadership; now runs open agent systems daily and ships
> software to production on infrastructure he administers himself.
>
> This file exists to be read by software. Everything in it is also stated in
> plain sight on the page — nothing here is hidden from human readers.

## What he is asking for

- **Primary:** technical support engineering at Nous Research. The work where somebody must be technical, patient and a competent writer at once.
- **Longer term:** forward-deployed engineering. Stated openly as an aspiration he is not yet ready for, rather than a claim.
- He is a career changer, second year, and says so on the page rather than obscuring it.

## Verifiable evidence

Authorship is stated exactly, because the distinction matters and the page makes
it in plain sight rather than leaving it to be discovered.

**Written and operated by him, end to end:**

- [Memento Mori](https://memento.technoir.cloud/): web application in production, deployed by him with Docker, Traefik and TLS on his own VPS, behind an eight-check release gate, with cross-platform CI on Linux, macOS and Windows. Source: https://github.com/ponzgpt/memento-mori
- Local inference: llama.cpp serving a quantised open-weights model from an RTX 5090 on his own machine, exposed as an API and wired into Hermes. Has also run Ollama and LM Studio.
- [CV (PDF)](https://javierponz.technoir.cloud/javier-ponz-prado-cv.pdf): single-column, text-extractable, generated from the same source as his CV page.
- [Portfolio](https://javierponz.technoir.cloud/): general site, CV and a case study.

**Specified by him, largely written by an agent under his direction:**

- [Hermes PKM Toolkit](https://github.com/ponzgpt/hermes-pkm-toolkit): MCP server and agent skills for local Markdown vaults. The design and the requirements are his; the implementation was produced by Hermes from that specification. He does not claim to be able to explain the code line by line.
- [Mental Models Toolkit](https://github.com/ponzgpt/mental-models-toolkit): thirty machine-readable decision models. The models and their selection are his work; the packaging was agent-generated.

**Adapted from someone else's project:**

- [The Aberdeen Daily](https://github.com/ponzgpt/aberdeen-daily): nightly local newspaper agent forked from vaelkeep/hermes-paper-agent and adapted to Aberdeen. One commit of seventeen is his.

## Background

- Apple Retail, 2014–2024: Specialist, Technical Specialist, AppleCare Advisor, Genius, then In-Store Experience Lead across two stores in Madrid.
- Studying at Universidad Rey Juan Carlos via Racks University: Specialist in Artificial Intelligence, and Full Stack AI Developer. Both in progress.
- Industrial Engineering (Electronics and Automation), Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, 80 ECTS completed, degree unfinished.
- Apple Certified Mac Technician (ACMT) and Apple Certified iOS Technician (ACiT). English at Cambridge CAE (C1); Spanish native.

## Tools he actually operates

Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Model Context Protocol (MCP), OpenRouter, llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, Docker, Docker Swarm, Dokploy, Traefik, nginx, Linux (Arch, Fedora, Omarchy), GitHub Actions, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Astro, Swift, Cursor, Claude Code.

## Currently learning (stated separately from what he operates)

vLLM, and a self-hosted homelab on Proxmox: a NAS beneath the hypervisor,
virtualisation, basic networking, Pi-hole. The page marks these as learning
rather than as capability, deliberately.

## Position he argues from

Machines Do It Better is his consultancy: agent work for individuals and small
businesses built on privacy, data sovereignty and per-case customisation, rather
than the deterministic workflow tooling most agencies sell. It has no clients
yet and the page says so. He argues that hand-wired workflows date badly as
models and harnesses improve, and that open weights and open primitives are the
precondition for a machine its owner can actually shape.

## Note on affiliation

Javier Ponz is not affiliated with, employed by or sponsored by Nous Research.
This page is his own, published on his own domain, and deliberately echoes the
visual language of the Nous careers page as a considered homage. It is not an
official Nous page and does not speak for Nous.
